claims.text: The frozen KG has 6,814 concepts. The course map puts each concept under one lecture; the lessons give each concept one owning topic.
Rule A (the first lecture with an introduces COVERS edge) crowded column 1: lecture 1 is an overview that introduced SVM, backpropagation and other later topics.
Under v1, 61 of the 464 covered concepts land in lecture 1, more than in any other lecture.
Rule B (at least 2 supporting passages, the most passages win) put PCA in lecture 4 from a 2-mention Q&A aside.
PCA has 2 mentions in lecture 4, 1 in lecture 18 and no defining passage in any lecture, so under v3 no lecture reaches weight 3.
Rule v3: a DEFINES passage counts 3, a MENTIONS passage 1; below weight 3 a lecture cannot claim the concept; a defining lecture beats a mentioning one; the earliest wins a tie.
233 of 464 covered concepts are placed. Lecture 4 now holds probability distribution, out-of-sample error, squared error, error measure, noisy target and noise.
Our re-run of the v3 rule on the frozen KG files places 232 of 464; its lecture 4 holds all six concepts the note names.
The one-concept gap to the app's 233 is likely the app's rule that a concept mapped to a placement concept is always on the map.
A passage that mentions a concept is weak evidence that it teaches it: weight definitions above mentions and set a minimum support.
First lesson rule: a topic owned a concept only when its core book sections held at least 34 % of all the concept's DEFINES passages.
VC dimension has 19 defining passages: 5 in lectures, 11 in no topic, 6 in the vc-dimension topic. No topic reached 34 %, so the VC-dimension lesson was never suggested.

Current rules, any one gives ownership: (a) lecture-video passages count toward their topic and the share is taken over passages in some topic; (b) a full name match with a seed topic's title wins; (c) a small alias table of 6 entries.
The ownership file adds a fourth rule: an explicit override gives a concept one owner, and it wins.
Owned concepts went from 1,565 to 1,821 or more; learn-first links appear on 29 of 40 seed topics (was 14).
The ownership file in use today lists 1,818 distinct owned concepts over 84 topics.
Very broad concepts stay unowned on purpose: generalization error, precision, partition function, degrees of freedom and the central limit theorem.
In today's file generalization error still has no owner; the central limit theorem and partition function now belong to topics added after the course.
A learn-first link needs at least 2 KG edges because PREREQUISITE_OF is still about 8 % wrong in a blind sample; a single edge shows as a lighter see-also link.
The two products use different ownership rules for the same KG; one shared, tested module would stop drift (provisional).
The rules belong in chapter 3 as design rules from the KG to the learner-facing views; they do not touch the C2 experiment, whose arms read the frozen KG directly.
A lesson built for one student's gap by an agent inside the app was a feasibility study only: researched, not built, with no plan to build it now.
The cross-book topic map aligns 2,828 TOC sections of 9 books and the 18 CS 156 lectures; a check of 10 topics gives precision 0.81 strict and 0.98 lenient; recall was not measured.

claims.loc: Log: all 84 lessons authored; later frozen
claims.text: 84 lessons in all: the 40 seed topics in lecture order plus 44 topics after the course; all 84 are authored.

A full lesson is a short video, an interactive on real data, the same idea side by side in each book, practice items and the sources; a source opens the book at the page with the section highlighted, or the lecture video at the minute.
The VC-dimension interactive tests every dichotomy of 3 to 5 dragged points exactly (m(4) = 14 < 16) and draws the CS 156 digits 1 vs 5 learning curve against the VC bound.
Videos are Manim scenes rendered off the Mac on a Kaggle CPU kernel; the finals run 36 to 48 seconds.
Every explain layer, takeaway, caveat, video and interactive carries the page or lecture moment it comes from, or says it is ours; the build fails on an item with neither.
A model of another family (Codex) refutes each batch from our own files, with no book text sent; every finding is adopted or kept with a reason.
In the app, a lesson renders its blocks in their pinned order; widgets run in a sandboxed iframe; a missing video shows "video pending".
Ask about this fills the chat box with the selected excerpt (at most 600 characters) and sends nothing; the answer still cites retrieved passages only.
Lesson practice is scored on the server; bands are green at 80 % or more, yellow 50-80 %, red under 50 %; practice never enters the placement model.
Every answered turn carries Learn more: up to 3 lessons for the concepts the question and the answer name, with no model call (1-44 ms).
The placement result recommends lessons for red and yellow concepts only, and the Lessons page shows them under For you.
On the concept map, each concept lists every destination: a full lesson as Lesson, a reading fallback as Sources.
The tutor reads the lessons-site build read-only; without that folder the lesson pages are hidden.
The lessons run locally: the lesson server binds 127.0.0.1 and streams PDFs and videos from this machine; no book text is in git.
A companion is one page per chapter: a reading map, then for each key idea Watch (Manim, 60-120 s), Touch and Check, plus one Play sandbox when the topic allows.
Companions use our own words, figures and code; quotes are at most 25 words with the page; book text never leaves the machine.
Checks: the claim's anchor on its page (script), a model of another family on claim and page, and an 8-word copy check against the chapter.
Codex found 26 problems in a pilot draft that passed every script check: the scripts prove attribution and originality, not correctness.
Phase 1: 12 central-chapter companions on the shared kit, Codex refutation with 135 findings all dispositioned, one Kaggle-rendered Manim video each.
A full run has followed phase 1 (Essential GraphRAG and others); the companions folder holds 32 chapter pages.
Planned: companions share the tutor's unit ids and relations; key ideas become Concept nodes, Check items become non-gold exercise rows, Watch and Touch become assets keyed by concept.
A companion is the chapter-keyed view and a lesson the concept-keyed view of the same Watch, Touch, Check and Read blocks (provisional, design only).
Version 2, lessons written by an agent, is not built.
The course map has one column per CS 156 lecture and a Background column; each column shows its 6 most connected concepts plus every concept a placement concept maps to.
The per-lecture DEFINES and MENTIONS counts and the v1, v2 and v3 outcomes shown for each concept come from our re-run on the frozen KG files.
Placement now has a concept for every lecture; concepts with no lesson topic are matched to a lesson by their lecture.
The pilot companion is Hands-On Large Language Models, chapter 3, Looking Inside Large Language Models (pp. 73-107).
The pilot companion has a reading map, 6 widgets, a KV-cache anatomy figure and a Manim preview.
